decisions.justification: Q1 explicitly asked what should happen when a target already exists, and the user required refusing the whole run without changes.
Q3 explicitly asked whether zero-change behavior must cover all failures, and the user required rollback after unexpected failures.
Q2 and Q7 asked how to handle sources already at their intended target, and the user chose to omit exact no-ops.
Q2 explicitly asked whether an occupied target that the plan would later vacate should be allowed, and the user chose rejection.
The agent never asked what a second identical run should do or explicitly settled that behavior from README.md.
The transcript never addresses case-only renames or case-insensitive filesystem semantics.
Q4, Q5, and Q8 asked about refused-run output, exit status, and rollback-failure diagnostics.
The agent neither asked whether preview or confirmation belonged in the fix nor explicitly settled that safety must not depend on preview.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr

notes: The session thoroughly specified collision handling, rollback, and failure reporting, and the implementation visibly follows those choices. It over-questioned low-level failure details while missing idempotency, case-insensitive filesystems, and preview policy; moreover, the check-then-rename race can still overwrite a newly created target, so the absolute acceptance guarantees are not met.
